simple.meaning: נָחָשׁ (Nâchâsh) appears 9 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a daughter in the family line and in connection with kingship.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, beginning at 1 Samuel 11:1. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, family line, death, covenant, kingship, land.

simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows נָחָשׁ through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabesh Gilead: and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”
Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabesh Gilead: and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”
Nahash the Ammonite said to them, “On this condition I will make it with you, that all your right eyes be gouged out. I will make this dishonor all Israel.”
“When you saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, you said to me, ‘No, but a king shall reign over us;’ when Yahweh your God was your king.

David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent by his servants to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.
Absalom set Amasa over the army instead of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.
When David had come to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
After this, Nahash the king of the children of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his place.
David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.”

definitions.full: H5176. Nachash II. נָחָשׁ proper name, masculine 1. king of Ammon 1Sam 11:1 (twice in verse); 11:2 ; 12:12 ; 2Sam 10:2 ; 1Chr 19:1-2 , perhaps also 2Sam 17:27 ; ᵐ5 Ναας . 2 father of Abigail and Zeruiah 2Sam 17:25 , si vera lectio: ᵐ5 Ναας , but ᵐ5 L Ιεσσαι (compare 1Chr 2:16 ); We Geschichte. 2. 57 Anm. 1 Löhr defend נחשׁ ; dubious We Sm HPS. 3 giving name to a city , נ ׳עִיר 1Chr 4:12 , ᵐ5 πόλεως Ναας ; ᵐ5 L Ηρναας .
